strengths: Addresses an important gap in MLLM capabilities for 3D generation with well-motivated problem formulation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple metrics (p-FID, p-KID, CLIP-IQA+, MUSIQ), ablations, and user studies (~2,400 data points)
Unified architecture enabling transfer learning between generation and understanding tasks, with demonstrable improvements in 3D captioning
Honest and thorough discussion of limitations, failure cases, and gaps versus state-of-the-art methods
Thoughtful architectural design with hybrid causal-parallel masking and mode-binding (sequential vs. parallel) rather than task-binding
weaknesses: Significant performance gap versus state-of-the-art non-MLLM methods: p-FID of 12.55 versus TRELLIS's 7.36 (nearly 2× worse), undermining practical utility
Limited technical novelty: primarily recombines existing components (Qwen3-VL backbone, Hunyuan3D-2.1 VAE, MoT framework from Liang et al. 2025) without novel techniques
Core technical mechanism inadequately specified: 'Shared Causal-Parallel Self-Attention' lacks mathematical formulation and implementation details; token routing between branches undefined

Reproducibility significantly hindered: no code/model release mentioned, requires 16 NVIDIA H20 GPUs, finicky VAE preprocessing with reconstruction issues handled via workaround rather than principled solution
Misleading 'end-to-end' framing: still relies on Hunyuan3D-2.1's external VAE decoder; not truly end-to-end generation

3D understanding evaluation limited to image-based inputs with MLLM-generated captions (typically <20 words), making assessment of true 3D spatial understanding incomplete; performance lags specialized methods like ShapeLLM-Omni
Token budget (4k tokens) still modest and limiting compared to methods using 10× more tokens for geometric detail
Unfair baseline comparisons due to using newer/larger Qwen3-VL without clear scale normalization; quadratic inference cost scaling limits practical deployment

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation with multiple metrics (p-FID, p-KID, CLIP-IQA+, MUSIQ) and user studies (~2,400 data points), demonstrating methodological rigor
Thoughtful technical design including hybrid causal-parallel masking and 3D-aware positional encoding that specifically addresses 3D representation needs
Honest and detailed discussion of limitations including data preprocessing effects, frozen VAE constraints, and performance gaps with commercial systems
Demonstrates that joint training for 3D generation transfers positively to 3D understanding capability, providing useful insights for multimodal learning
Achieves best performance among MLLM-based 3D generation methods (outperforms SAR3D and ShapeLLM-Omni)
weaknesses: Significant and unresolved performance gap with non-MLLM methods: TRELLIS achieves 1.7× better p-FID (7.36 vs 12.55) and 4.5× better p-KID (0.12 vs 0.27). The practical value of MLLM integration is unclear when specialized methods substantially outperform it

Limited architectural novelty: explicitly inspired by concurrent work (Liang et al., 2025; Shi et al., 2025); claimed distinctions (model-based binding, vision-centric init, positional encoding) are incremental engineering choices rather than conceptual advances

Weak 3D understanding results: trails established methods on captioning (Table 2); critically, training uses MLLM-generated synthetic captions rather than ground-truth annotations, undermining genuine 3D understanding

Unjustified architectural constraints: frozen VAE (why not fine-tune?), VAE reconstruction issues forcing change from mixed to uniform point sampling, and AdaLN failure indicating potential architectural instability

High inference cost (35-45 seconds for 4096-5120 tokens) with quadratic runtime scaling; requires expensive infrastructure (16 H20 GPUs); reproducibility concerns due to missing code and implementation details

Unclear value proposition: if goal is 3D generation, specialized methods are superior; if goal is unified understanding, the 3D understanding gap (trailed by PointLLM, 3D-LLM) is problematic. The integration lacks empirical justification
Data quality issues: synthetic MLLM-generated captions, data preprocessing reduces precision, token budget (4k) is 10× fewer than high-resolution methods, test set limited to toys4k subset
Incomplete experimental comparisons: no head-to-head evaluation of CG-MLLM vs. TRELLIS/CraftsMan on identical benchmarks; unclear if Table 1 comparisons use identical test sets
Limited failure analysis: only 2 failure cases shown; no quantitative failure rates or systematic mode analysis

Hybrid masking mechanism and transformer interaction procedure lack detailed technical explanation; claim that omitting intra-block embeddings preserves permutation invariance lacks rigorous justification

strengths: Well-motivated dual-transformer architecture (TokenAR/BlockAR) that effectively addresses computational efficiency for 3D generation in MLLMs
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple metrics (p-FID, p-KID, CLIP-IQA+, MUSIQ, CLIP) with fair comparisons to both MLLM-based and non-MLLM methods
Thorough ablation studies demonstrating the impact of individual components (VAE backbone, MOT architecture, LLM backbone, token budget, scaling)
Honest discussion of limitations, failure modes, and performance gaps, particularly acknowledging inability to surpass non-MLLM SOTA
Novel observation that training for 3D generation improves 3D understanding, suggesting bidirectional transfer in multimodal models
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (particularly Figures 1, 4-5, 11) and helpful scaling analysis (Tables 3-5)
Practical architectural improvements over prior MoT methods, including vision-centric initialization strategy and 3D-aware positional encoding
weaknesses: Limited fundamental novelty: paper primarily demonstrates effective integration of existing components (Qwen3-VL + Hunyuan3D2.1-VAE + MoT) rather than proposing novel techniques; core innovation is architectural engineering rather than methodological
Does not achieve overall SOTA: p-FID of 12.55 is 71% higher than TRELLIS (7.36), and claims are narrowed to 'SOTA among MLLM-based methods,' significantly limiting practical impact
Problematic VAE dependency: Section 4.4 reveals Hunyuan3D2.1-VAE produces distorted reconstructions with ad-hoc workaround (using only uniform points); impact on quality ceiling not analyzed
Insufficient justification for design choices: downsampling factor (20×), latent dimension (64), conditional discard schedule (90%→10%), learning rates lack ablations or principled motivation
Incomplete technical clarity: Shared Causal-Parallel Self-Attention mechanism lacks implementation details; masking patterns in Fig. 3 difficult to interpret; noise scheduler unexplained
Limited user study rigor: only 100 questionnaires without protocol details, annotator selection info, or inter-annotator agreement; no statistical significance testing of quantitative results
3D understanding improvements are modest relative to specialized methods (Table 2): 13.51 BLEU-1 vs ShapeLLM-Omni-7B's 18.51, with unclear fairness of comparison due to different training data
Reproducibility concerns: no code availability mentioned, training duration/exact dataset size not specified, only one training curve shown, some implementation details require reverse-engineering
